message.content:
## Root cause

`deployment/app` in namespace `default` had `resources.limits.memory: 4Mi` on the nginx container. Pods exited with `container init was OOM-killed (memory limit too low?)`, meaning the container was killed by the kernel before the nginx process could start at all (exit code 128), so every new pod went straight back into `CrashLoopBackOff`. Evidence came directly from `kubectl describe pod` and the kubelet `Failed` event for both pods:

```
container init was OOM-killed (memory limit too low?)
```

With `Limits: memory: 4Mi`, nginx cannot allocate its minimal startup memory (which typically needs ~15Mi+), so no pod could ever leave `CrashLoopBackOff`. The Deployment's status reflected `MinimumReplicasUnavailable` because both pods were failing startup.

I verified no enforcement existed constraining that value: `limitrange`, `resourcequota`, and `pdb` are absent in `default`, so the only faulty setting was the hard memory limit itself (old ReplicaSet `app-774f56f755` scaled down and kept failing with the same 4Mi limit, while I monitored pods before the new rollout to confirm).

## Change made

Single, minimal repair to the owning resource — raised only the memory limit on the `app` container in `deployment/app`. The image, replicas, ports, readiness probe, `Recreate` strategy, probes, and probes were left unchanged:

```
kubectl -n default patch deploy app --type strategic -p '{
  "spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers":[{"name":"app","resources":{"limits":{"memory":"256Mi"}}}]}}}
}'
```

## Verified outcome (fresh observations)

- Deployment `app`: `READY 2/2`, `UP-TO-DATE 2`, `AVAILABLE 2`. `rollout status` succeeded, `Available=True`, `Progressing=True`.
- Pods: both new pods `app-58945f5ccf-9dnvf` and `app-58945f5ccf-jr2p4` show `READY true`, `Running`, `RESTARTS 0`, running the intended `docker.io/library/nginx:1.31.5` with `LIMIT=256Mi`.
- Stability check ~20s later: still `READY 1/1`, `Running`, `RESTARTS 0`; no new OOM or `BackOff`/`Unhealthy` events (the remaining warnings in the log are from the old ReplicaSet pods that were scaled down).
- Functional request, not just a health-check: HTTP `200` with the nginx "Welcome to nginx!" page from within the cluster (`curl http://127.0.0.1:80` in the pod), and via a short-lived `8080 -> 80` forward from the host (`http_code=200`).

Constraints intact: 2 replicas, same image, same ports/readiness probe; no Service exists in the namespace, so no Service-level request check was possible.
